content_html:
git blame tells you who wrote the line. This tells you why.

What is this?

When you build software with AI agents (Claude Code, Codex), the reasoning — what you asked for, what the agent decided, which alternatives were rejected — lives in session transcripts on your disk. gitwhy turns those transcripts into three useful things:

  • A visual report: click any file in your project and see the conversations that created it, in order — you asked → the agent reasoned → the commit.
  • A safety copy of all your transcripts, because Claude Code deletes them after 30 days by default — silently, with no undo (#59248, #62476).
  • A small memory file (GITWHY.md) your agents read at the start of each session, so they already know why the code is the way it is instead of re-discovering it every time.

One Python file. No dependencies. 100% local — nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Graph and origin-story view from a 200-session benchmark history — or skip the screenshots and click around the live demo. Your real project's report shows your real files and your real conversations.

Try it in 60 seconds

No setup, no data needed — just Python 3.9+:

python gitwhy.py --demo

Open the gitwhy-report.html it creates. That's the tool, running on sample data. Now do it for real:

# 1. Protect your history FIRST (copies every transcript to ~/.gitwhy/archive)
python gitwhy.py archive

# 2. Build the report for any project you've used Claude Code or Codex in
python gitwhy.py /path/to/your/repo

This writes three files next to your code:

file who it's for what it is
gitwhy-report.html you interactive graph + per-file origin stories
GITWHY.md your AI agents compact "why each file exists" memory
gitwhy.json scripts & tools the same provenance as structured data

Works the same on Windows (python gitwhy.py C:\Users\you\project), macOS, and Linux.

Stop the deletions at the source

Do this once. In ~/.claude/settings.json:

{ "cleanupPeriodDays": 3650 }

⚠️ Do not use 0 — a known bug makes 0 stop transcripts being written at all (#23710).

Feed it to your agent

GITWHY.md is written for agents. Both Claude Code and Codex automatically read an instructions file from your repo root at the start of every session — you point that file at the digest once, and from then on every session begins already knowing why your code is the way it is.

Claude Code — add this line to your repo's CLAUDE.md (create the file if it doesn't exist):

Before exploring this codebase, read GITWHY.md — it explains why each file exists
and which sessions/commits shaped it.

Codex CLI — the same line, in AGENTS.md at the repo root.

That's the whole setup. What the agent then reads looks like this:

## src/auth.py  · layer: service
- 2026-04-01 [claude] refactor the auth flow to use short-lived tokens with refresh rotation
- 2026-04-03 [codex] fix token refresh race on concurrent requests
- commit aa61cae: Add refresh-token rotation with family revocation

The digest costs roughly ~130 tokens per file, so even a large project's entire "why" fits in a few thousand tokens — instead of the agent burning far more re-deriving intent with grep/read loops every single session. (The · layer: tags appear when an Understand-Anything graph is present — see below.)

Keep it fresh: re-run python gitwhy.py . after a work session, or automate it with a git post-commit hook — create .git/hooks/post-commit containing:

#!/bin/sh
python gitwhy.py . > /dev/null 2>&1

(then chmod +x .git/hooks/post-commit on macOS/Linux). Every commit regenerates the digest, so the memory your agent reads is never stale.

For tools rather than agents, the same provenance ships as gitwhy.json — see "What can I build on gitwhy.json?" below.

Plays well with Understand-Anything

If your repo has a committed Understand-Anything knowledge graph (.ua/ — the 73k⭐ codebase mapper), gitwhy detects it automatically and merges the two views: their structure (layers, functions, classes, summaries) appears alongside its provenance in every file's panel, and their relationships render as structure edges in the graph. No setup — run their /understand once, then run gitwhy as normal. Validated against plugin v2.9.4. Without it, gitwhy works exactly the same, just structure-free.

What can I build on gitwhy.json?

The JSON has a simple shape:

{
  "repo": "myproject",
  "files": {
    "src/auth.py": [
      { "date": "2026-04-01", "agent": "claude",
        "prompt": "refactor the auth flow to use short-lived tokens" }
    ]
  },
  "commits": { "src/auth.py": "aa61cae" }
}

Ideas people can build in an afternoon: a CI bot that comments each PR with the origin story of the files it touches; provenance-aware search over your codebase; "which files did we change for feature X?" scripts. It's also the foundation the planned MCP server will query. If you build something on it, open an issue — I'd love to see it.

How the linking works

gitwhy connects sessions to commits using three stacked signals, strongest last:

  1. File overlap — files edited in the session (from Edit/Write tool calls in Claude Code, apply_patch payloads in Codex) vs. files changed in each commit (git log --numstat)
  2. Time windows — the commit happened during (or shortly after) the session
  3. In-session commits — a git commit command visibly executed inside the session transcript; this is near-certain evidence

Each file edit is attributed to the prompt that caused it, paired with the agent's adjacent reasoning. Login errors, rate-limit noise, and CLI commands are filtered out; duplicated/resumed transcripts are collapsed by content fingerprint.

Supported agents

Agent Transcripts read from Status
Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl ✅
OpenAI Codex CLI ~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl ✅
Cursor / Gemini CLI — roadmap — adapters welcome; see parse_codex_session for the pattern

Honest limitations

  • Linking is heuristic. The three signals catch the common case well, but unusual workflows (committing days later from another terminal, moving a repo so absolute paths change) will thin the links.
  • Reasoning excerpts are real quotes chosen by adjacency, not AI summaries — occasionally the excerpt isn't the best quote from the session.
  • Already-deleted transcripts are gone. gitwhy can't resurrect what the cleanup already removed; it can only make sure it never happens again.

Roadmap

  • MCP server so agents can query provenance ("why does this function exist?")
  • Cursor and Gemini CLI adapters
  • Auto-archive on session end via agent hooks
  • Optional --translate pass rendering content translations alongside the verbatim originals (originals always kept — provenance stays verbatim)
  • Graph: time-axis layout and label physics for very dense projects

Benchmarks

Measured by benchmark_gitwhy.py on a consumer Windows laptop (synthetic histories with realistic multi-MB transcripts dominated by tool output, real git repos, exact token counts via tiktoken cl100k_base):

scale sessions commits transcripts parse+link render raw corpus GITWHY.md compression
SMALL 10 24 0.1 MB 0.17 s 0.03 s 20,149 tok 2,157 9×
MEDIUM 60 150 0.6 MB 0.78 s 0.02 s 161,000 tok 8,018 20×
LARGE 200 300 79.5 MB 2.47 s 0.05 s 13,762,575 tok 16,156 852×

Honest framing: compression measures the digest against the raw history it summarizes — a ceiling, not a measured per-session saving inside a live agent. Run it yourself: python benchmark_gitwhy.py (install tiktoken for exact counts).

FAQ

How is this different from Claude Code's /compact? Different jobs. /compact is working memory: it summarizes the current conversation, inside one session, and its summary dies with that session's transcript. gitwhy is long-term memory: it spans all sessions and both agents, links reasoning to durable artifacts (commits, files), lives in your repo, and archives the raw transcripts. /compact is RAM; gitwhy is disk.

How is this different from CLAUDE.md? CLAUDE.md is instructions, written by a human, about how the agent should behave now — and it goes stale unless someone updates it. GITWHY.md is memory, generated from history, about why the code became what it is — and it regenerates from the transcripts, so it can't go stale. They work together: your CLAUDE.md simply points the agent at GITWHY.md.

Is this a knowledge graph? It's a provenance graph — sessions, commits, and files as nodes with produced/touched edges — built deterministically from transcripts and git log. Every edge is a verifiable fact and costs zero LLM tokens to build. It is not (yet) a semantic knowledge graph — no entity extraction or embeddings. That query layer is the MCP-server roadmap item.

Why are the report's quotes in English even when I switch the UI to فارسی? The language switcher translates the interface (labels, dates, hints). The quotes are history — the exact words you and the agent used, preserved verbatim. A provenance tool that rewrote your past conversations would be falsifying the record it exists to protect. If your sessions happened in Persian, your quotes display in Persian, RTL and all.

Tests

python test_gitwhy.py    # builds Claude + Codex fixtures in a sandbox, 18 checks

License

MIT — see LICENSE.

Built because I lost months of my own research context to the 30-day cleanup and decided that should never happen to anyone again.

— Mehrta (Fateme) Eslami · mehrtam.github.io

content_html_zh:
gitblame 告诉你这行代码是谁写的。 这告诉你原因。

这是什么？

当您使用 AI 代理（Claude Code、Codex）构建软件时，推理（您的要求、代理的决定、哪些替代方案被拒绝）都存在于磁盘上的会话记录中。 gitwhy 将这些记录转化为三个有用的东西：

  • 可视化报告：单击项目中的任何文件，然后按顺序查看创建该文件的对话 — 您询问 → 代理推理 → 提交。
  • 所有成绩单的安全副本，因为默认情况下 Claude Code 会在 30 天后删除它们 — 默默地、无法撤消 (#59248、#62476)。
  • 您的代理在每个会话开始时读取一个小内存文件 (GITWHY.md)，因此他们已经知道为什么代码是这样的，而不是每次都重新发现它。

一个 Python 文件。 没有依赖性。 100% 本地 - 任何地方都不会上传任何内容。

来自 200 个会话基准历史记录的图表和起源故事视图 - 或跳过屏幕截图并单击实时演示。 您真实项目的报告显示您的真实文件和真实对话。

60 秒内尝试一下

无需设置，无需数据 — 只需 Python 3.9+：

python gitwhy.py --demo

打开它创建的 gitwhy-report.html。 这就是在样本数据上运行的工具。 现在就真正去做吧：

# 1. Protect your history FIRST (copies every transcript to ~/.gitwhy/archive)
python gitwhy.py archive

# 2. Build the report for any project you've used Claude Code or Codex in
python gitwhy.py /path/to/your/repo

这会在您的代码旁边写入三个文件：

file 这是给谁的 它是什么
gitwhy-report.html you 交互式图表+每个文件的原始故事
GITWHY.md 你的人工智能代理 紧凑的“为什么每个文件存在”内存
gitwhy.json 脚本和工具 与结构化数据具有相同的出处

在 Windows (python gitwhy.py C:\Users\you\project)、macOS 和 Linux 上的工作方式相同。

从源头停止删除

这样做一次。 在~/.claude/settings.json中：

{ "cleanupPeriodDays": 3650 }

⚠️ 不要使用 0 — 一个已知的 bug 会导致 0 停止写入记录 (#23710)。

将其提供给您的代理

GITWHY.md 是为代理编写的。 Claude Code 和 Codex 在每个会话开始时都会自动从您的存储库根读取指令文件 - 您将该文件指向摘要一次，从那时起，每个会话都开始知道为什么您的代码是这样的。

Claude 代码 — 将此行添加到您的存储库的 CLAUDE.md 中（如果该文件不存在，则创建该文件）：

Before exploring this codebase, read GITWHY.md — it explains why each file exists
and which sessions/commits shaped it.

Codex CLI — 同一行，位于存储库根目录的 AGENTS.md 中。

这就是整个设置。 代理读取的内容如下所示：

## src/auth.py  · layer: service
- 2026-04-01 [claude] refactor the auth flow to use short-lived tokens with refresh rotation
- 2026-04-03 [codex] fix token refresh race on concurrent requests
- commit aa61cae: Add refresh-token rotation with family revocation

每个文件的摘要成本大约为 130 个令牌，因此即使是一个大型项目的整个“原因”也可以容纳几千个令牌，而不是代理在每个会话中使用 grep/read 循环燃烧更多的重新派生意图。 （· 层：当出现 Understanding-Anything 图时，标签就会出现 — 见下文。）

保持新鲜感：重新运行 python gitwhy.py 。 工作会话结束后，或使用 git post-commit hook 自动执行 — 创建 .git/hooks/post-commit ，其中包含：

#!/bin/sh
python gitwhy.py . > /dev/null 2>&1

（然后在 macOS/Linux 上 chmod +x .git/hooks/post-commit）。 每次提交都会重新生成摘要，因此您的代理读取的内存永远不会过时。

对于工具而不是代理，与 gitwhy.json 具有相同的出处 — 请参阅“我可以在 gitwhy.json 上构建什么？” 以下。

与 Understanding-Anything 配合得很好

如果您的存储库有一个承诺的 Understanding-Anything 知识图（.ua/ — 73k⭐ 代码库映射器），gitwhy 会自动检测它并合并两个视图：它们的结构（层、函数、类、摘要）与其出处一起出现在每个文件的面板中，它们的关系在图中呈现为结构边缘。 无需设置 - 运行 /understand 一次，然后正常运行 gitwhy。 已针对插件 v2.9.4 进行验证。 没有它，gitwhy 的工作原理完全相同，只是没有结构。

我可以在 gitwhy.json 上构建什么？

JSON 具有简单的形状：

{
  "repo": "myproject",
  "files": {
    "src/auth.py": [
      { "date": "2026-04-01", "agent": "claude",
        "prompt": "refactor the auth flow to use short-lived tokens" }
    ]
  },
  "commits": { "src/auth.py": "aa61cae" }
}

人们可以在一个下午建立的想法：一个 CI 机器人，可以用它所涉及的文件的起源故事来评论每个 PR；对代码库进行出处感知搜索； “我们为功能 X 更改了哪些文件？” 脚本。 这也是计划中的 MCP 服务器查询的基础。 如果你在上面构建了一些东西，请提出一个问题——我很乐意看到它。

链接如何运作

gitwhy 使用三个堆叠信号将会话连接到提交，最强的最后一个：

  1. 文件重叠 - 在会话中编辑的文件（来自 Claude Code 中的 Edit/Write 工具调用、Codex 中的 apply_patch 有效负载）与每次提交中更改的文件 (git log --numstat)
  2. 时间窗口 - 提交发生在会话期间（或之后不久）
  3. 会话中提交——在会话记录中明显执行的 git commit 命令；这是近乎确定的证据

每个文件编辑都归因于导致它的提示，并与代理的相邻推理配对。 过滤掉登录错误、速率限制噪音和 CLI 命令；重复/恢复的转录本按内容指纹折叠。

诚实的限制

  • 链接是启发式的。 这三个信号很好地捕捉了常见情况，但不寻常的工作流程（几天后从另一个终端提交，移动存储库以便绝对路径发生变化）会使链接变薄。
  • 推理摘录是邻接选择的真实引言，而不是人工智能摘要——有时摘录并不是会议中的最佳引言。
  • 已经删除的成绩单不见了。 gitwhy 无法恢复清理已删除的内容；它只能确保这种情况不再发生。

FAQ

这与 Claude Code 的 /compact 有什么不同？ 不同的工作。 /compact 是工作记忆：它总结了一个会话中当前的对话，并且其摘要随该会话的记录一起消失。 gitwhy 是长期记忆：它跨越所有会话和两个代理，将推理链接到持久工件（提交、文件），存在于您的存储库中，并存档原始记录。 /compact 是 RAM； gitwhy是磁盘。

这与 CLAUDE.md 有什么不同？ CLAUDE.md 是由人类编写的关于代理现在应该如何表现的指令 - 除非有人更新它，否则它就会过时。 GITWHY.md 是从历史中生成的记忆，关于代码为何会变成现在的样子——并且它从记录中重新生成，因此它不会变得陈旧。 它们协同工作：您的 CLAUDE.md 只需将代理指向 GITWHY.md。

这是知识图谱吗？ 它是一个来源图——会话、提交和文件作为具有生成/触及边缘的节点——根据转录本和 git 日志确定性地构建。 每条边都是可验证的事实，构建成本为零 LLM 代币。 它（还）不是语义知识图——没有实体提取或嵌入。 该查询层是 MCP 服务器路线图项。

为什么即使我将 UI 切换到 فف٢٠，报告的引用还是英文？ 语言切换器翻译界面（标签、日期、提示）。 这些引言都是历史——你和代理人使用的确切词语，逐字保存。 重写你过去对话的出处工具将伪造它所保护的记录。 如果您的会话以波斯语进行，您的报价会以波斯语、RTL 等形式显示。
